extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, and USPTO examiners (audience for CRU procedures)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and content requirements, limits, and substantive tests governing ex parte reexamination, supplemental examination, and reissue filings and proceedings before the USPTO Central Reexamination Unit (CRU). Intended to guide filing, examination, and related strategic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexamination: Anyone. Supplemental examination: Patent owner. Reissue: Patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes eligibility/standing for initiating each type of proceeding; supplemental examination and reissue are owner-only remedies, while ex parte reexamination requests may be filed by third parties or owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible basis for ex parte reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must be based upon patents and printed publications only (37 CFR 1.510).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested, must be in writing, and must be accompanied by the applicable fee. If filed by a third party, service on the patent owner and certain certifications are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for an ex parte reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: Request must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested, be accompanied by a reexamination fee, and (if third party) include certifications of service and estoppel status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.510 et seq. implement these requirements; failure to show pertinency/manner of application is a common basis for denial. The request may be filed at any time during the patent's period of enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question (SNQ) determination for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner determines whether a 'substantial new question of patentability' (SNQ) affecting any claim exists; an SNQ can be raised by patents/printed publications presented in a new light (PTA 2002). Decision on a request must be made no later than 3 months from its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an SNQ is found an order for ex parte reexamination is issued. The 3-month decision clock is statutory; SNQ analysis may consider previously examined references if re-presented with new reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party filing certifications for ex parte requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If filed by a third party, the request must include a certification that a copy of the request has been served on the patent owner (37 CFR 1.33(c)) and a certification that estoppel provisions under 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) or 325(e)(1) do not prohibit the requester from filing the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These certifications are mandatory for third-party requests; failure to certify service or estoppel may be fatal to the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) and 325(e)(1) estoppel effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner in an IPR or PGR that results in a final written decision, or its real party-in-interest or privy, may not request or maintain a proceeding before the Office with respect to that claim on any ground that the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during that IPR or PGR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a final written decision issues in an AIA proceeding, petitioner/real party-in-interest/privy are barred from later filing ex parte reexamination on grounds that were or could have been raised. See MPEP 2214.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's discretionary denial under 35 U.S.C. 325(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if an SNQ is found, the Director may deny reexamination if the same or substantially the same prior art or arguments were previously presented to the Office; during pendency of a post-grant review the Director may stay, transfer, consolidate, or terminate matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 325(d) provides discretion to avoid repetitive proceedings. This is a key gatekeeping tool where prior submissions to the Office make reexamination unnecessary or redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner statement and third-party reply timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If reexamination is ordered based upon a third-party request, the patent owner may file a statement within two months from mailing date of the order including proposed narrowing amendments; the third party may file a reply within two months of the patent owner's statement. If the patent owner waives the right to file a statement, the third party may not file a reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties have limited involvement: after the allowed reply they may not file further papers in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte nature and 'special dispatch' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination proceedings are ex parte and must proceed with 'special dispatch' within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party requester will be sent copies of Office actions and the patent owner must serve responses on the requester, but the substantive prosecution is ex parte after the reply period; 'special dispatch' means accelerated internal handling per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of evidence considered in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations, or other written evidence explaining contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications may be considered in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These evidentiary submissions can clarify dates or content but cannot introduce new categories of prior art beyond patents and printed publications for ex parte reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment limitation in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of a claim cannot be enlarged by amendment in a reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only narrowing or confirmation amendments are permitted; broadening amendments are prohibited in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination conclusion: NIRC and reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination concludes with issuance of a Notice of Intent to Issue a Reexamination Certificate (NIRC); the reexamination certificate is part of the issued patent and will list cancellations, confirmations, patentable amended/new claims, statutory/terminal disclaimers, and any claims not reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reexamination certificate formally records the outcome of the proceeding and modifies the patent accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) by filing a notice of appeal and may seek judicial review at the CAFC; third-party requesters may not appeal or participate in the patent owner's appeal and may not seek judicial review of any decision favorable to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties have limited appellate/judicial rights vis-à-vis reexamination outcomes that favor patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined reexamination fee reduction conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Half-price filing fees (50% reduced) apply to ex parte reexamination requests having 40 pages or less that meet certain format requirements per 37 C.F.R. § 1.20(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlined reexamination applies only when format/length conditions are met; fee relief is statutory/regulatory and not automatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes reexamination discontinued
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination was replaced by inter partes review (IPR) effective September 16, 2012; no new inter partes reexamination requests may be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legacy inter partes reexaminations may remain pending, but post-2012 challengers use IPR/PGR mechanisms rather than inter partes reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may request supplemental examination to consider, reconsider, or correct information believed to be relevant to the patent; it concludes with a certificate indicating whether the information raises an SNQ of patentability. If an SNQ is indicated, an ex parte reexamination is ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination is an owner-initiated process to cleanse the record and can trigger reexamination when SNQ exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination can shield against inequitable conduct findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental examination potentially shields patent owners from a finding of unenforceability due to inequitable conduct for the information considered and subject to a written decision by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 77 Fed. Reg. 48828 (Aug. 14, 2012). The shield applies only to information properly presented and considered in the supplemental examination and reflected in the Office's written decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for a supplemental examination request (37 CFR 1.610(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Must identify the patent number and each claim for which supplemental examination is requested; include a list of all items of information (no more than 12 items per request); list prior or concurrent post-patent Office proceedings; provide a separate, detailed explanation of relevance and manner of applying each item to each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also must include a copy of the patent, copies of each item of information with English translations of necessary parts, a summary for documents over 50 pages, and identification of owners plus a 37 CFR 3.73(c) submission establishing entirety of ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit of 12 items in supplemental examination request
rubrics_metrics.description: Each request for supplemental examination may include no more than twelve items of information believed to be relevant to the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests exceeding 12 items must be split; careful selection/organization of items is important to avoid multiple filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination procedural limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination whether an SNQ is raised generally occurs within 3 months; determination limited to items identified in the request as applied to identified claims and based on claims in effect at the time; no amendments accepted and no interviews conducted during supplemental examination; the proceeding concludes with issuance of a supplemental examination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner must promptly notify the USPTO of any federal court decision involving the patent while supplemental examination is pending or after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences when supplemental exam certificate finds an SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: If the certificate states an SNQ is raised, ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 257 will be ordered. In such reexamination the patent owner will not have the right to file a patent owner statement, reexamination may be conducted on the basis of any item of information (not limited to patents/printed publications), and issues beyond patents/printed publications may be considered. Information material to patentability is defined by § 1.56(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental-exam-triggered reexamination is broader in permissible evidence than ordinary ex parte reexamination and limits owner procedural rights (no owner statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue purpose and basic constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue permits errors in the original patent to be corrected, permits claims to be broadened if a broadening reissue is filed within two years of issuance of the original patent, may correct inventorship, but not all errors are correctable (see 35 U.S.C. §§ 251 & 252; MPEP §1401-1470).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue is an owner-initiated corrective vehicle subject to strict statutory timing and substantive limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for filing a reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: Required items include fees, a reissue 'specification' (the printed patent), a reissue oath or declaration, and consent of assignee to filing & statement of ownership when the patent is assigned (see Form PTO/AIA/50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include required paperwork or proper ownership/consent statements will render the filing defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath or declaration must point out error(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oath/declaration must point out the error(s) being corrected—only one error need be given—and must specifically identify how the error renders the patent wholly or partly inoperative or invalid. Reissue applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, are not required to state that all errors arose without deceptive intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'error' requirement is central: reissue corrects 'error' in the original patent; the description must be specific about the nature and effect of the error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration signature rules (general and for broadening reissue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oath/declaration must include 37 CFR 1.63 requirements and generally must be signed by the inventors. For broadening reissue (37 CFR 1.175): the oath/declaration must identify at least one claim sought to be broadened and all inventors are required to sign except in limited exceptions (e.g., original application filed under 1.46 by the assignee on/after 9/16/2012 or use of substitute statement under 1.64). If there are no broadened claims, the assignee of entire interest may sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature/authority rules vary depending on whether scope is being broadened; missing inventor signatures for broadening reissue are typically fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior oath/declaration for continuing reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: For a continuing reissue application, a copy of the inventor’s oath/declaration from the earlier-filed post-AIA reissue parent application may be used provided the inventor executed the earlier oath, the continuing reissue does not seek to enlarge the scope of the original patent claims, or the original application was filed under 37 CFR 1.46 by the assignee of the entire interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids re-signing in limited continuing-application situations; be careful about scope-expansion restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee consent and 37 CFR 3.73 ownership statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent is assigned, the assignee must consent to filing the reissue even where the oath/dec is signed by the inventor(s). Consent must be signed by an authorized party and supported by a 37 CFR 3.73 statement establishing ownership; recordation alone is not sufficient—§3.73 statement must be filed in the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without proper consent and a compliant 3.73 statement, the oath/declaration is incomplete and the reissue filing may be defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue specification and drawings requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue specification (including claims) is filed in double-column format (copy of printed patent). Original drawings: clean copies of printed patent drawing sheets are filed as the formal drawings; new drawing sheets are required for any new or amended figures (see 37 CFR 1.84 and 1.173).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting proper formatted specification and correct drawing changes is necessary for a compliant reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: No need to surrender original patent when filing reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants do not need to physically surrender the original patent when filing a reissue application (MPEP §1416 and 37 CFR 1.178(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative convenience: original patent remains in owner's possession; surrender is not required at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: General limitations on reissue eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue may correct errors such as error in scope of claims, inventorship, priority to foreign application, benefit claim to domestic application, error in drawing or specification, and error in filing terminal disclaimer. Expired patents are not eligible for reissue; term cannot be extended by eliminating 35 U.S.C. §120 benefits; subject matter surrendered to obtain the original patent cannot be recaptured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue is limited in subject matter and term effects; review MPEP §1402 for detailed examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-year limit on broadening reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: No broadening of claim coverage is permitted unless a broadening reissue application was filed within two years from the grant of the original patent (35 U.S.C. §251(d)). Intent to broaden must be established in the reissue application within two years; a reissue filed within two years for other reasons may not be broadened later after the two-year date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict statutory two-year bar; courts and MPEP require timely assertion of intent to broaden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for 'Broadened Reissue Claim' (broadening meaning)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amended/new claim in the reissue that contains within its scope any conceivable invention that would not have infringed any of the claims of the original patent (i.e., causes previously non-infringing subject matter to now infringe) constitutes a broadened reissue claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use factual inquiry (Would previously non-infringing inventions now infringe?) and consult case law (Tillotson, In re Self) and MPEP §1412.03(I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapture prohibition in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee cannot recover via broadening in reissue subject matter surrendered in an effort to obtain allowance of the original patent claims (recapture rule). Deliberate withdrawal/amendment to obtain allowance is not considered an 'error' correctable by reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recapture is a substantive bar even within the two-year window; see 3-step recapture test in MPEP §1412.02 and relevant case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3-step test for impermissible recapture
rubrics_metrics.description: 1) Determine whether and in what respect the reissue claims are broader than the original claims; 2) Determine whether the broader aspects relate to subject matter surrendered in original prosecution; 3) Determine whether reissue claims were materially narrowed in other respects related to surrendered subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this test (MPEP §1412.02) to analyze recapture issues; materially narrowing limitations must be related to surrendered subject matter to avoid recapture (see In re Mostafazadeh).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-elected claims cannot be recovered via reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims were non-elected in the application that became the patent and were not re-filed in a divisional, they cannot be recovered via reissue—failure to file a divisional is not an 'error' correctable under 35 U.S.C. §251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic implication: lost or non-elected claims require divisional practice rather than reissue recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original-patent requirement for reissue (same invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue claims must be for the same invention as disclosed as being the invention in the original patent per 35 U.S.C. 251. To seek a 'new' invention by reissue, the specification must clearly and unequivocally disclose the newly claimed invention as a separate invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue cannot be used to claim an invention not clearly disclosed in the original patent; satisfy 'original patent requirement' or risk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing reissue claims permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application may add one or more claims that are narrower than one or more broader existing patent claims; adding narrower claims without amending or canceling the broader patent claims may be correctable by reissue (e.g., In re Tanaka). The declaration may be signed by the assignee instead of inventor(s) in some situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrowing reissue is an accepted use of reissue to correct overbroad claims or add fall-back positions, subject to signature/ownership rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of co-pending reexaminations and reissues
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-pending proceedings may be stayed or suspended, merged (Reexam/Reexam or Reexam/Reissue—where reissue rules apply), or examined concurrently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU practice includes options to stay/suspend/merge and to examine co-pending matters together; strategic coordination with PTAB or other Office units may influence timing and outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU monitoring and interplay with PTAB/AIA proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRU closely monitors pending and concluded PTAB post-grant proceedings and reviews all PTAB determinations before taking action in an ex parte reexamination proceeding or pending reissue application involving the same patent. Considerations include 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) estoppel, 35 U.S.C. 325(d) discretionary denial, 37 CFR 42.73(d)(3) patent owner estoppel, and conflicting positions on claim construction or prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AIA allows multiple types of challenges; CRU must account for estoppel and possible duplicative arguments when deciding whether to proceed with reexamination or reissue activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register notice re: amendments during pending AIA trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice (Apr 22, 2019) summarizes existing Office practice regarding claim amendments by patent owner through reissue or reexamination during a pending AIA trial, and summarizes factors the PTAB considers in determining whether to stay or suspend reissue/reexamination proceedings and when to lift such stays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice outlines coordination and factors considered when Office proceedings overlap with PTAB trials; consult notice for policy on amendments during AIA trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative post-grant mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Other post-grant mechanisms include certificate of correction (patent owner), disclaimers (patent owner), and AIA trial petitions (third party) such as IPR and PGR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate post-grant tool based on the error/issue to be corrected and the desired remedy (e.g., certificate of correction for clerical errors vs reissue for substantive claim corrections).
